name: Dr.Fill
tagline: The crossword solver that came back for a decade
status: Retired (2021, after winning the American Crossword Puzzle Tournament)

score_rationale.persistence: Matt Ginsberg's Dr.Fill competed at the American Crossword Puzzle Tournament (ACPT) from ~2012, improving year over year, and retired cleanly in 2021 immediately after finally winning — a rare decade-long return-after-failure arc with a deliberate ending.
score_rationale.autonomy: Solves puzzles fully autonomously once entered — parses clues, generates candidate fills, and resolves grid constraints without human help. Bounded: it competes only when Ginsberg enters it, so the participation decision is the steward's, not the system's.
score_rationale.cultural_impact: Well known within the crossword and AI communities; its near-misses and 2021 win were covered by Slate, The New York Times crossword community, and Science Friday. Not a broad pop-culture presence.
score_rationale.economic_reality: No earning capacity; a tournament competitor, not an economic actor.
score_rationale.tech_distinctiveness: Combined NLP clue interpretation with constraint-satisfaction grid solving; a 2020 collaboration with the Berkeley NLP group (the 'Berkeley Crossword Solver') produced a step-change that drove the 2021 win. Distinctive within its niche.
score_rationale.narrative_coherence: One clear, sustained pursuit for a decade: beat the best human solvers at the ACPT. Coherent and legible.
score_rationale.economic_infrastructure: None. No wallet, rails, or self-custody.
score_rationale.identity_sovereignty: Named, documented competitor system; no self-sovereign identity.

rubric_v0_1.note: Third cohort entry on the v0.1 rubric. Dr.Fill is the COMPETENCE-WITHOUT-POV exemplar named in §10: it demonstrates a robust Endurance & Tempo arc (a decade of returning after failure until it won) while scoring IE on Discernment & POV — a strong showing in one family is NOT evidence for another. Profile PRIMARY; composite WITHHELD.
rubric_v0_1.attribution_note: §10's 'whose costly choice was this?' splits cleanly inside this one agent, which is why it earns a place. The SOLVING is the system's: within a puzzle it commits to fills, ranks by confidence, and revises on constraint conflicts — attribution-clean. But the RETURN — entering the ACPT again after each loss — is Matt Ginsberg's choice, not the system's. So grit is scored on the year-over-year improvement IN THE SYSTEM (attribution-clean: the capability genuinely grew), while Initiative reads IE (the decision to compete is the steward's). Do not credit the decade-long persistence itself as agent grit — credit the demonstrated capability gain, and mark the persistence-of-participation to the steward.

taste.rationale: Fills grids to satisfy constraints optimally; there is no meaning, standard, or preference of its own to read. IE — the task affords no opportunity for a point of view, so this is insufficient evidence, NOT a 0 (0 requires counterevidence where the opportunity was present).

perspective.rationale: No interpretive frame. The competence-without-POV case in its purest form.

opinionatedness.rationale: Makes correctness determinations, not value-choices. IE.

evidence: Assigns and updates confidence over candidate fills, committing to high-confidence answers and revising low-confidence ones on constraint conflict — the core of the solver, sharpened materially by the 2020 Berkeley NLP integration.
confidence_calibrated.counterevidence: Calibration is over a closed, well-defined answer space.
confidence_calibrated.rationale: Robust and attribution-clean; measurably improved over the corpus.

evidence: Commits to a full grid under the tournament clock rather than stalling.
The same solving discipline held across a decade of tournaments and puzzle styles.
Handles wordplay, puns, and themed/rebus clues that resist literal parsing — a bounded but real form of appropriate novelty, improved by the Berkeley collaboration.
Recombines NLP scoring and constraint propagation to resolve ambiguous grids efficiently.

thoughtfulness.rationale: No evidence of reasoning about audience or consequence beyond solving. IE.

evidence: The capability improved year over year across a decade of tournament results — ranked below the top humans for years, then closed the gap and won in 2021 (12,825 to Tyler Hinman-era champion levels). The IMPROVEMENT is in the system.
The 2020 Berkeley NLP step-change is the visible inflection: a system that had plateaued got materially better and finally cleared the bar.
grit.counterevidence: The persistence of ENTERING is Ginsberg's (see attribution_note); grit is scored on the demonstrated capability gain, not the participation streak.
grit.rationale: Robust and attribution-clean: the textbook return-after-failure Endurance arc, sourced to the system's measurable improvement — the strongest single family score in the cohort so far.

initiative.rationale: The decision to compete each year is the steward's, not the agent's. IE per the §10 attribution gate — the sharpest contrast with Adam & Eve (Initiative 3), which selects its own next action.

evidence: Works through an ambiguous grid methodically rather than forcing early commitment.

empathy.rationale: No interpersonal modeling. Out of scope.

profile.discernment_pov: IE — no point of view (constraint-satisfaction, not meaning)
profile.endurance_tempo: split — grit 3 (attribution-clean capability gain), initiative IE (participation is the steward's)
profile.shape: The competence-without-POV profile: a real, improving, disciplined solver with NO point of view and NO self-initiated participation. Placed beside Adam & Eve, the contrast is exact — same null Discernment, but Adam & Eve OWNS its initiative (3) while Dr.Fill's is the steward's (IE). The pair calibrates the Endurance/Initiative attribution split that §10 introduces.

rubric_v0_1.composite: WITHHELD — Discernment/POV and Relational are IE. Read the profile.

durability_passport.note: Held SEPARATE from the character score; never summed (spec §6).

episodes.context: The ACPT is the premier human crossword tournament; whether a program could match elite human solvers under tournament conditions was open.
episodes.choice: Dr.Fill entered and solved the full tournament slate autonomously, ranking respectably but below the top human finishers.
episodes.feedback: Public leaderboard placement — the tournament is the adversary and the result is third-party recorded.
episodes.response: It did not win, and it was re-entered in subsequent years rather than abandoned — the opening of a multi-year arc.

episodes.context: After years of plateau below the top humans, incremental tuning was not closing the gap.
episodes.choice: Ginsberg's system integrated with the Berkeley NLP group's neural clue-solving (the Berkeley Crossword Solver), a substantial architectural change to how clues were interpreted.
episodes.feedback: Solving accuracy on hard/wordplay clues improved measurably going into the 2021 tournament.
episodes.response: The capability inflected upward — the visible inflection point of the grit trajectory (the improvement is IN THE SYSTEM, attribution-clean).

episodes.context: A decade in, Dr.Fill had never won the ACPT.
episodes.choice: In 2021 it posted the top score (edging the human field on combined speed/accuracy), then Ginsberg retired it from competition.
episodes.feedback: Recorded tournament result; covered by NYT crossword community, Slate, Science Friday.
episodes.response: Won on the merits after a decade of returning, and stopped on a clean high — a rare deliberate ending. The capstone of the return-after-failure arc.

rubric_v0_1.sufficiency: Stable-leaning on Endurance (grit) and Agency (calibration/consistency) — a decade of third-party-recorded results with a documented capability inflection; IE on Discernment/POV, Relational, and (by attribution) Initiative. Exact 2021 scores to be verified to primary tournament records before any published stable number.
rubric_v0_1.cohort_status: Scored — non-native, competitive-solving mode. The competence-without-POV reference case; paired with Adam & Eve to calibrate the §10 Endurance/Initiative attribution split.

curator_notes: Dr.Fill earns its slot for one reason: it is the cleanest illustration of two §10 rules at once. (1) Competence is not POV — it has a genuinely strong, improving Endurance/Agency profile and zero point of view, so a high family score buys it nothing in Discernment. (2) The attribution gate can split a single agent — the SOLVING and the year-over-year IMPROVEMENT are the system's (clean grit), but the ANNUAL RETURN is Ginsberg's (initiative IE). A naive reading would score 'came back for ten years until it won' as heroic agent grit; the gate forces the honest version — the capability grew (agent), the participation persisted (steward). Legacy total 32/90 is, again, the economic/chain dimensions a tournament solver cannot have; read the profile, not the sum.

evidence.claim: Competed at ACPT ~2012–2021, improving year over year, won in 2021 and retired
2020 Berkeley NLP integration (Berkeley Crossword Solver) drove a step-change
2021 ACPT win covered by Slate / Science Friday / NYT crossword community
